rogue.summary: The rogue is the best match in the set. The hood, the face, and the gold clasp read the same as in the mockup.
strengths: The dark inside of the hood frames the light face. This is the strongest focal point in the set.
The hair stays inside the hood and does not go through it.
The gold clasp, the ring buckle, and the hem stitches are small, clear accents.
issues: From the side, the hood is very deep, so the back of the head looks too large.
The mockup tunic is dark and has a pointed hem. The model tunic is short and plain.
The cape is longer and flatter than in the mockup, where the hem curls.
next: Make the back of the hood 10 to 15 percent shallower.
Add the darker, pointed lower tunic from the mockup.

archer.summary: The archer matches the mockup well. The floppy hood point, the elf ears, and the bow make a clear archer silhouette.
strengths: The hood point falls to the right side, as in the mockup, and breaks the outline.
The quiver with gold fletching reads from the back and in the sprites.
The face uses the rogue's construction, so the two heroes look like one set.
issues: The bow is smaller and darker than the large recurve in the mockup. It reads weakly in the front view.
The tunic and the cream leggings are shorter than in the mockup, so the legs look stubby.
The rim of the hood opening is thick and makes the face look small.
next: Make the bow 20 percent larger and use a lighter wood color.
Make the hood rim thinner.

knight.summary: The knight is very close to the mockup. The helmet, the red plume, the heart shield, and the red cape all read clearly.
strengths: Steel, gold, and red cloth read as clearly different materials.
The plume and the shield give a strong silhouette from every view.
The face stays visible under the helmet, and the gold brow band frames it.
issues: The mockup helmet has cheek guards that frame the face. The model has ear discs only, so the face looks wider.
The lower body is plain grey. The mockup has more shape and trim on the legs and the skirt.
At 65,228 triangles, the knight is the heaviest model. The mail and the plume use many triangles.
next: Add small cheek guards to the helmet.
Move all of the mail ring pattern into the normal map if the triangle count must go down.

wizard.summary: The wizard reads as a fire mage at once. The large hat and the fire staff match the mockup, but the robe is simpler.
strengths: The large red hat with the bent point is the signature shape. It reads in every sprite direction.
The flame on the staff and the flame in the palm are two glowing accents.
The teeth sit inside a dark rim, so the open smile reads as a mouth.
issues: The hat brim is flat. In the mockup, the brim is wider and droops at the front and the back.
The robe is one plain red mass. The mockup robe has gold trim, a flared cape, and a patterned skirt.
The flame on the staff is smaller than the large fireball in the mockup.
In the walk, the long robe hides the legs and does not swing, so the motion looks stiff.
next: Give the hat brim a soft droop.
Add gold trim and a flared hem to the robe.
Make the staff flame 30 percent larger.
Add a small swing to the robe hem in the walk and the run.

cleric.summary: The cleric has the beard, the hammer, the holy book, and the tabard of the mockup. The head does not match: it looks bald and young.
strengths: The big ginger beard with braids is the focal point, as in the mockup.
The hammer with the gold cross and the book make a clear cleric silhouette.
The steel pauldrons, the blue tunic, and the leather read as different materials.
issues: The hair starts high on the head, so the large bare forehead looks bald. In the mockup, the hair comes down to the brows.
The face is a child's face with a beard. The mockup dwarf has a larger nose, heavier brows, and a stronger jaw.
The mockup shoulder armor has gold trim, and the boots are big. The model armor is plain silver.
The hands are bare skin. The mockup shows leather gauntlets.
next: Bring the hairline down to the brows and add the braided top of the hair.
Make the nose larger and the brows heavier.
Add gold trim to the pauldrons and leather gauntlets to the hands.

druid.summary: The druid reads as the mushroom girl at once. The spotted cap, the basket, the potion, and the lantern staff all match the mockup.
strengths: The spotted cap is a strong and unique silhouette in every view.
The basket of mushrooms fills the back view, and the lantern swings on its own bone.
The fine hair and the cap gills are in the normal map, so the model stays light.
issues: The cap is smaller and flatter than in the mockup, where it is very large and shows a wide cream underside.
The hair is a straight bob with even bangs. The mockup hair is short and messy.
The front is plain. The mockup has belt pouches, small potions, and a clover emblem on the apron.
In the side sprite, the cap hides the face.
next: Make the cap 15 percent larger and tilt it back so that the underside shows.
Break the bangs into uneven locks.
Add the belt pouches and a potion at the hip.

adventurer.summary: The adventurer matches the main parts of the mockup: the teal bandana, the grin, the big pack, the map, and the short sword.
strengths: The pack with the bedroll and the lantern makes a clear traveler silhouette from the side and the back.
The red neckerchief is a strong color accent under the face.
The open grin has teeth and a tongue inside a dark rim, and it reads at 128 px.
issues: The hair is a tall, smooth mass with painted dark stripes. The mockup hair is messy, with many separate locks.
The mockup pack is a soft, round rucksack. The model pack is a box.
The map in the right hand reads as a pale stick in the front view.
next: Replace the painted hair stripes with grooves and more separate locks.
Make the pack rounder and softer.
Unroll the map a little so that it reads as paper.

goblin-warrior.summary: The goblin warrior is close to the four-view design in every view. The big ears, the angry eyes, and the dagger read at once.
strengths: The broad leaf ears are the silhouette from the front, the side, and the back.
All identity cues of the design are present: the nicked left ear, one shoulder guard, the diagonal strap, the pouch, the wraps, and the dagger.
The face reads at 128 px, and the attack jab reads in the side sprites.
It is light for a character: 31,138 triangles.
issues: The tuft on the head has three thin spikes. The design shows one soft crest.
The design shows the pouch from the back too. The model pouch is at the front of the hip, so it does not show from the back.
The belt buckle is smaller than the large tan buckle in the design.
next: Merge the tuft into one soft crest.
Make the belt buckle 30 percent larger.

horned-boar.summary: The horned boar is rebuilt in the chibi style from a new mmx mockup. It is all head and shoulders: a huge angry head, a pink snout, upturned tusks, and cream horns.
strengths: The eyes, the horns, the tusks, and the pink snout read in all eight sprite directions.
The black brows slope down toward the snout, so the face reads as angry but cute.
It keeps everything the bench brief asks for: tusks, a bristle mane, glowing eyes, and the walk, charge, and idle clips. It also has a new gore attack.
It is light: 26,188 triangles.
issues: From the side, the head looks smaller than in the mockup, because the snout is short in profile.
The horns are thinner at the tips than the thick crescents in the mockup.
The small teeth show only as a row under the snout. The mockup shows a wider open grin.
next: Make the snout 20 percent longer so that the head reads larger from the side.
Thicken the horn tips.

goblin-archer.summary: The goblin archer matches the mockup's pointed hood, big ears, war paint, and leather gear. It shares the warrior's face and body, so the two goblins read as one tribe.
strengths: The pointed dark hood with the ears through it is a strong, unique silhouette in every view.
The dark hood frames the light face, and the red fletching over the shoulder is a clear second accent.
The shot clip reads in the side view: the goblin turns, raises the bow, draws, and looses.
issues: The mockup holds the bow across the body in both hands. The model holds it upright at the side, because that reads better in sprites and allows the shot clip.
Seen from above in the sprites, the hood rim covers the brows, so the face reads weaker than the warrior's face.
In the shot clip, the drawing hand is hard to see, because it stays behind the body.
The mockup has a long back cape. The model has only the short capelet, so that the quiver shows.
next: Pull the drawing hand further out to the side in the shot clip.
Add a nocked arrow during the shot, so the draw reads at 128 px.

skeleton.summary: The skeleton warrior matches the enemy-sheet design: a grinning skull with angry glowing eyes under a riveted iron helmet, a red scarf, mail, a raised sword, and a round red shield.
strengths: The slanted black sockets with amber eyes, the heart-shaped nose hole, and the square teeth make a clear angry skull face.
Iron, steel, mail, bone, red cloth, wood, and brass read as different materials.
It shares the knight's body and legs, so the armored characters look like one set.
issues: The mockup shows a dynamic lunge. The model stands in the set's neutral pose.
From above, the dark helmet dome is the largest shape in the sprites, and the face shows only in the front directions.
In the chop, the wind-up is small, so most of the motion is in the downward cut.
The mockup helmet is lighter steel with dark patches. The model helmet is dark iron all over.
next: Raise the sword higher in the wind-up of the chop.
Make the helmet steel lighter, with the patina in patches.

orc-warrior.summary: The orc warrior is a stocky brute that is all shoulders and arms, with a heavy scowl, big tusks, a topknot, a spiked pauldron, and a hand axe, as in the mmx mockup.
strengths: The yellow eyes under heavy black brows, the big tusks, and the pointed beard make a strong scowl at 128 px.
The wide shoulders, big bracers, and spiked pauldron give it a heavier silhouette than the goblins, so the two kinds read apart.
The heavy walk shifts the weight from side to side, and the axe chop has a high wind-up.
issues: The hair stripes look like a knit cap. The mockup hair is combed back in thick strands.
The loincloth is two plain red flaps. The mockup has a shaggy, torn red cloth.
The skin is a little brighter and greener than the olive skin in the mockup.
next: Replace the painted hair stripes with shallow grooves that sweep back to the topknot.
Give the loincloth more torn points and a darker, shaggier edge.

bandit.summary: The bandit matches the mmx mockup: wild dark hair, an angry glare over a dark red mask, a striped shirt under a leather vest, a loot sack, and a curved cutlass.
strengths: The glare between the dark hair and the red mask is a strong focal point, and it reads in the front sprites.
It uses the rogue's head and skeleton, so it fits with the heroes, but the mask, the stripes, and the sack make it read as a different person.
The sack and the mask tails swing on their own bones in the walk and the slash.
issues: From above, the big hair covers the brows a little in the sprites.
The mockup vest has more straps and a second pouch. The model vest is plain.
The loot sack sits behind the arm, so it shows less from the front than in the mockup.
next: Move the sack a little to the side, so it shows more from the front.
Add a strap with a buckle to the vest.

zombie.summary: The zombie matches the mmx mockup: grey-green skin, one bulging yellow eye and one glossy black eye, a toothy grimace, a patched shirt, a rope belt, torn trousers, and sandals.
strengths: The mismatched eyes are a unique signature, and they read in every sprite direction that shows the face.
The shamble drags one foot and keeps the arms reaching forward, so the motion reads as a zombie at once.
It uses the rogue's head and skeleton, so it reads as a villager who came back wrong.
issues: The hair is a smooth black mass with thick locks. The mockup hair is thinner and messier.
The shirt is plain. The mockup shirt has a torn collar, loose threads, and buttons.
The torn trouser hems are painted. The mockup shows deep, shaggy tears.
next: Make the hair locks thinner and more varied.
Add a few loose threads at the collar and the hem.

slime.summary: The slime is the slime king from the enemy sheet without its crown, cape, and chain: a glossy green jelly dome with a grumpy glare, settling into a puddle with round drips.
strengths: The squash and stretch sells the jelly: it stretches on each hop, flattens on landing, and the slam leaps and lands flat.
The slanted jelly lids and heavy brows give the same grumpy glare as the mockup.
It is very light: 7,354 triangles. The color is one constant, so the P2 fire, ice, and poison slimes can reuse the file.
issues: From behind and from the side, it is a plain green dome, so the silhouette gives little to remember.
The mockup jelly looks translucent, with bubbles inside and floating around it. The model is opaque, with only three pale bubble spots.
The mouth is a small, faint line.
next: Add two or three small bubbles that float around the slime on their own bones.
Make the frown bolder, so it reads at 128 px.

dire-wolf.summary: The dire wolf matches the mmx mockup: a huge scowling head with cream brows, amber eyes, and a toothy grin, framed by cheek tufts, tall ears, and a full cream ruff, on a compact body with a bushy tail.
strengths: The pointed ears, cheek tufts, and ruff make a spiky outline that reads in every sprite direction.
The cream brows and muzzle around the amber eyes give a strong focal point on the dark face.
The trot moves the diagonal leg pairs together, and the bite has a clear crouch, lunge, and snap.
issues: The mockup sits in a compact crouch. The model stands on four straight legs, so the body looks longer from the side.
The fur is one smooth dark grey. The mockup fur has more value variation on the legs and the back.
The cream muzzle is still narrower than the wide grinning muzzle in the mockup.
next: Paint a slightly lighter grey on the chest and the lower cheeks.
Widen the cream muzzle toward the cheeks.

giant-spider.summary: The giant spider takes the mmx mockup's glaring red eyes, pale fangs, and chunky orange-banded legs, with the big abdomen moved behind the head so it reads as a spider from every side.
strengths: It reads as a spider in all eight sprite directions, and the orange skull on the abdomen is a strong mark from behind.
The purple and orange palette with red eyes is unique in the set and easy to spot.
The four-leg alternating gait and the rear-up strike both read in the side view.
issues: I changed the mockup's anatomy on purpose: its round body sits under the head, and here it sits behind. So the front view is less like the mockup.
Seen from above in the sprites, the brow shelf hides much of the big eyes, and the four small eyes read as red dots.
The body is one smooth fuzz texture. The mockup has more shape in the head, such as a ridged brow.
next: Tilt the head up a little, so the big eyes show more in the top-down sprites.
Give the small eyes white eyeballs, as in the mockup.

dragon-fire.summary: The fire dragon matches the mmx mockup closely: a squat red dragon that is half head, with cream horns, a red and orange crest, heavy black brows, a toothy grin, spread orange bat wings, a ridged cream belly, and a finned tail.
strengths: The spread wings, horns, and crest make a unique silhouette that reads in all eight sprite directions.
The black brows over the yellow eyes and the white teeth in the dark grin give a strong focal point.
The roar reads well: it rears back with the wings raised, then lunges with the wings flared.
It has a fly clip: the body lifts and tilts forward, the wings beat through a full stroke, the legs dangle back, and the tail waves.
issues: The mockup puffs smoke from one nostril. The model has no smoke or fire effect yet.
The horns are thinner than the big cream horns in the mockup.
The cheek frills are small and hide behind the wings from the front.
next: Add a fire-breath effect as a separate effects asset, and play it with the roar.
Make the horns 20 percent thicker at the root.

blacksmith.summary: The blacksmith matches the mmx mockup: a burly smith with a black beard and a red bandana, a leather bib apron with brass rings and a buckled belt, big leather gloves, and a hammer resting on his shoulder.
strengths: The red bandana and black beard frame a friendly face that reads at 128 px in every direction.
The bib apron with straps, brass rings, and buckle reads as a smith's apron at once.
The work clip lifts the hammer and brings it down in front, onto an unseen anvil.
issues: He uses the rogue's large head, so he is less burly than the mockup, where the body is bigger than the head.
The short hair at the back of the head is one plain black mass.
In the work clip, the wind-up hides the hammer behind the head, so the lift reads weakly.
next: Make the chest and arms 10 percent bigger, so he reads as the strongest villager.
Raise the hammer higher in the wind-up of the work clip.

farmer.summary: The farmer matches the mmx mockup: a wide woven straw hat, a straw bundle in his mouth, rosy cheeks, a red plaid shirt, patched blue overalls with brass buttons, boots, and a tall pitchfork.
strengths: The wide straw hat and the upright pitchfork make a silhouette that reads as a farmer at once.
The red plaid and the blue denim are two clear color masses, with the straw hat as a light accent.
The work clip digs the fork into the ground in front and then lifts it high.
issues: From above, the wide hat hides much of the face in the sprites.
The mockup hat has a softer, floppier brim that tilts. The model brim is flat and even.
The hair shows as a smooth mass under the hat at the back.
next: Tilt the hat back a few more degrees, so the face shows more in the top-down sprites.
Give the brim a gentle wave.

guard.summary: The town guard matches the mmx mockup: a round steel kettle helmet with a crest, a big brown mustache, a sky-blue tabard with a gold tower and gold trim over mail, steel pauldrons and gauntlets, and a spear with a teal pennant.
strengths: The helmet, mustache, and spear with a pennant make a clear watchman silhouette in every sprite direction.
The blue tabard with the gold tower and trim reads as a town livery, and it differs from the knight's red.
The spear thrust levels the spear and drives it forward; the pennant flutters in the walk.
issues: The helmet sits lower than in the mockup, and the hair locks under the brim cover the top of the eyes.
From above, the big steel dome hides the face in the sprites.
The mockup pennant hangs down along the haft. The model pennant sticks out to the side.
next: Make the helmet dome 10 percent smaller, so more of the face shows.
Hang the pennant down and let the walk lift it.

skeleton-mage.summary: The skeleton mage matches the candle-skull caster on the Chibi Quest enemy sheet: a skull under a lit, melting candle, with glowing eyes in dark sockets, a torn purple robe, a skull necklace, a satchel, a purple flame in one hand, and a lantern staff.
strengths: The candle on the skull is a unique, memorable silhouette that reads in every sprite direction.
Three glowing accents (the candle flame, the palm flame, and the lantern) make it easy to spot in a dark dungeon.
The walk is a gliding shuffle under the robe, and the lantern swings on its own bone.
issues: The candle and the skull are both cream, so they merge into one tall block from the back and the side.
In the cast, the flame ends in front of the chest, under the big skull, so the push is short.
The robe's hem is torn, but it has fewer and shorter tatters than the mockup.
next: Make the wax whiter or the skull warmer, so the candle reads apart from the skull.
Give the cast a bright flare on the palm flame (scale it up at the moment of the cast).
